title: quercus sessiliflora subsp. kerneri
intro: Quercus sessiliflora subsp. kerneri, commonly known as the Kermes Oak, is a plant species in the beech family (Fagaceae) and is native to the Iberian Peninsula. The Kermes Oak has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which can help to reduce the risk of chronic diseases such as cancer and cardiovascular disease. The plant's bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, have been found to exhibit therapeutic actions such as antimicrobial, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory effects. Furthermore, the Kermes Oak has been traditionally used to treat various health conditions, including fever, digestive issues, and skin problems.
